items.title: Google puts Target and Albertsons grocery carts inside Search and Gemini
items.excerpt: Google began rolling out Connected Apps in US Search and the Gemini app for Albertsons, Safeway, Shaw's and Target: Gemini interprets a loose request, picks products and fills the retailer cart via the Universal Commerce Protocol. Experian and H&R Block also reached Search, with Angi and Thumbtack due in coming weeks.
items.rationale: A live US rollout that lets Gemini fill Target and Albertsons carts from Search, moving the point of sale into Google's AI surfaces right before the holiday peak.

items.title: Amazon draws 24% of retailer searches but 11% of AI shopping answers
items.excerpt: Verve data (Sep 1 - Nov 16) shows Amazon takes 24% of US retailer searches but is named in only 11% of AI shopping answers, while Target and smaller retailers are over-represented in AI answers relative to search share.
items.rationale: New Verve data shows AI shopping answers favor different retailers than search does, which gives brands a concrete reason to plan AI-answer visibility separately from search share.

items.title: 구글·팔란티어 부른 올리브영…"무한 스크롤 쇼핑시대 끝낸다"
items.excerpt: CJ올리브영이 첫 테크 콘퍼런스 '디파인 옴니'에서 상품 탐색부터 장바구니까지 AI가 처리하는 에이전틱 커머스 구상과 글로벌몰 AI 쇼핑 전략을 공개했다.
items.rationale: Korea's largest beauty retailer laid out an agentic-commerce plan in which AI handles product discovery through to the cart, a domestic retail signal for K-beauty brands selling through it.

items.title: Walmart mulls role advertising will play in an agentic shopping world
items.excerpt: On its Q3 call, Walmart said ad momentum (Walmart Connect) remains strong but executives acknowledged AI agents such as Sparky are producing different consumer behaviors, and weighed how ads will fit agent-led shopping.
items.rationale: The largest US retail-media seller says on the record that agents like Sparky are changing shopper behavior, and that matters to every Walmart Connect advertiser planning 2027 budgets.

items.title: OpenAI rewrites ChatGPT Business Hub terms after legal language raises concerns
items.excerpt: OpenAI revised its ChatGPT Business Hub terms after concerns that the original language could restrict businesses' legal claims - a new action on the hub where brands manage how they appear and run sponsored agents in ChatGPT.
items.rationale: OpenAI changed the terms brands accept to run business agents and sponsored placements in ChatGPT, so brands should check the new terms before they sign up.

https://digiday.com/media/openai-rewrite.new_action: OpenAI issued revised ChatGPT Business Hub terms of service (new legal terms replacing the original claim-restricting language), a new official change after the 11-11 business-agents launch
